title: Public Company Accounting Oversight Board; Notice of Filing of Proposed Rules on Amendments to Auditing Standards for Auditor's Use of the Work of Specialists (SEC Release 34-85435; contains PCAOB's statement of purpose, response to comments, and economic analysis for PCAOB Release No. 2018-006)
authors_or_organization: PCAOB (filed with U.S. SEC); published in Federal Register 84 FR 13442-13484
publication_date: 2019-04-04 (Federal Register); PCAOB adoption 2018-12-20; SEC approval 2019-07-01 (Release 34-86270); effective for FY ending on/after 2020-12-15
limitations: Regulator's own rationale and description; shows obligations and regulator-reported inspection observations, not compliance rates or effort. Inspection observations are from risk-selected (non-random) inspections. Full amended rule text (AS 1210, AS 1105 App. A) was not read verbatim; requirements are taken from the filing's description. pcaobus.org blocked scripted access so the PCAOB adopting release itself was not retrieved; the Federal Register filing reproduces its substance.

title: Interim Analysis Report: Evidence on the Initial Impact of New Requirements for Auditing Accounting Estimates and the Auditor's Use of the Work of Specialists (PCAOB Release No. 2022-008)
authors_or_organization: PCAOB Office of Economic and Risk Analysis staff
data_collection_dates: Firm survey Aug 2021; 31 engagement-partner interviews Aug 2021-Feb 2022; 12 audit committee chairs + 9 preparers Sep 2021-Mar 2022; inspections data pre/post FY2020
limitations: Regulator evaluating its own rule. Survey targeted firms/audits with heavy specialist use (explicitly non-random 'upper bound'); statistical analysis descriptive, not causal (no control group; COVID and other rule changes confound). Self-reported hours. Estimates and Specialists requirements implemented jointly, so effects not separable. Retrieved via WebFetch (binary saved by tool, converted locally).

title: ISA (UK) 620 (Revised June 2016): Using the Work of an Auditor's Expert
authors_or_organization: Financial Reporting Council (UK), based on IAASB ISA 620
limitations: UK-conformed version of IAASB ISA 620; quoted paragraphs (3, 8, 12-14, A33-A40) match the international text in substance but UK version was used because the IAASB PDF was not retrieved. Superseded by later UK editions and by IAASB narrow-scope amendments (Dec 2025); standard shows obligation, not practice.

title: Basis for Conclusions: Narrow-Scope Amendments to IAASB Standards Arising from the IESBA's Using the Work of an External Expert Project
limitations: Staff document, non-authoritative; only Sections A-D read. Concerns competence/capabilities/objectivity gating, not evaluation of content.

title: ASA 500 Audit Evidence (compiled, Dec 2022) - conforms with ISA 500
limitations: Only paragraph 8 (management's expert) read. Australian conformed text used as stand-in for IAASB ISA 500 para 8.

title: ASA 610 Using the Work of Internal Auditors (compiled, Dec 2023) - conforms with ISA 610 (Revised 2013)
limitations: Requirements paras 15-25 read; application material not read. Australian conformed text used as stand-in for ISA 610 (Revised 2013). PCAOB AS 2605 (US analog) not retrieved (pcaobus.org blocked).

title: ASA 402 Audit Considerations Relating to an Entity Using a Service Organisation (compiled, Dec 2023) - conforms with ISA 402
limitations: Definitions, requirements 13-21 and application paras A31-A38 read. Stand-in for ISA 402; US analogs AU-C 402 (AICPA) and PCAOB AS 2601 not retrieved (AS 2601 page returned HTTP 403). Standard shows obligation, not how user auditors behave.

title: Basis for Conclusions: ISAE 3402, Assurance Reports on Controls at a Service Organization
data_collection_dates: Exposure draft comment period (dates not recorded)
limitations: Staff document explaining standard-setter reasoning, non-authoritative. Reports respondent views qualitatively ('most', 'significant minority') without counts. Paras 41-46 and 65-66 read in full; rest skimmed.

title: Order Granting Approval of Amendments to Auditing Standards for Planning and Supervision of Audits Involving Other Auditors and Dividing Responsibility for the Audit with Another Accounting Firm (SEC Release No. 34-95488)
authors_or_organization: U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (approving PCAOB Release No. 2022-002)
limitations: SEC summary of PCAOB amendments; full PCAOB adopting release not read. Describes obligations, not practice.

title: Audits of Complex Estimates as Verification of Management Numbers: How Institutional Pressures Shape Practice
authors_or_organization: Emily E. Griffith; Jacqueline S. Hammersley; Kathryn Kadous
limitations: Abstract seen only as rendered/paraphrased by a fetch tool (IDEAS page); verbatim abstract and full text not reviewed. Interview study (24 auditors per abstract summary), pre-2020 standards. source_type is interview-based field study (no closer category).

title: Auditors, Specialists, and Professional Jurisdiction in Audits of Fair Values
limitations: Abstract seen via fetch-tool rendering of IDEAS record; two verbatim passages from the working paper are available only as quoted by the PCAOB in 84 FR 13472-13474 (secondary quotation). Published version not reviewed. Interview study of 28 auditors and 14 valuation specialists under pre-2020 standards. A related Griffith & Hammersley (2019) draft found during search is marked 'do not quote or cite without authors' permission' and was deliberately not used.

title: When Do Auditors Use Specialists' Work to Improve Problem Representations of and Judgments about Complex Estimates?
limitations: Only search-engine abstract excerpts and a university news article (fetched) were seen; participant counts, effect sizes and materials not reviewed.

title: Auditors' and Specialists' Views About the Use of Specialists During an Audit
authors_or_organization: J. Efrim Boritz; Natalia V. Kochetova(-Kozloski); Linda A. Robinson; Christopher Wong
limitations: access_status=other: only search-engine summaries of catalog abstracts seen; abstract not directly viewed (econbiz blocked by bot protection); full text not reviewed. Interview study: 34 practitioners (12 auditors, 22 tax/IT/valuation/forensic specialists) from six firms per catalog summary.

title: Current Practices and Challenges in Auditing Fair Value Measurements and Complex Estimates: Implications for Auditing Standards and the Academy
authors_or_organization: Steven M. Glover; Mark H. Taylor; Yi-Jing Wu
publication_date: 2017-02 (Auditing: A Journal of Practice & Theory 36(1):63-84); published online 2016-07
data_collection_dates: Survey (submitted Jan 2015; survey dates not located)
funding_or_commercial_relationships: Funded by the Center for Audit Quality (CAQ); CAQ Research Advisory Board helped refine survey
limitations: Copy obtained from a third-party academic aggregator (typeset.io); provenance of that copy uncertain. Survey of 32 partners/senior managers with FVM expertise at 5 firms (3 Big 4, 2 international networks); self-reported practice; open-ended responses coded (avg kappa 0.63); pre-2020 standards; small n.

title: Mind the Gap: Why Do Experts Have Differences of Opinion Regarding the Sufficiency of Audit Evidence Supporting Complex Fair Value Measurements?
authors_or_organization: Steven M. Glover; Mark H. Taylor; Yi-Jing Wu; Ken T. Trotman
limitations: Abstract seen via fetch-tool rendering of IDEAS record only; participant counts not reported there; full text not reviewed.

title: Auditing Challenging Fair Value Measurements: Evidence from the Field
authors_or_organization: Nathan H. Cannon; Jean C. Bedard
limitations: access_status=other: only search-engine summaries of the abstract seen; full text paywalled and not reviewed. Engagement-level field data reported by auditors; counts not seen.

title: Evidence Specificity and Auditors' Heuristic Responses to Human and Non-Human Specialists
authors_or_organization: Benjamin P. Commerford; Blake A. Holman
funding_or_commercial_relationships: Funded by the Center for Audit Quality (participants supplied via CAQ Research Advisory Board grant) and the University of Kentucky
limitations: Working paper version (peer-review status of this version not established; source_type closest category). Single hypothetical case (insurance claim reserve); 98 audit managers; DV is proposed adjustment (reliance), no ground-truth accuracy measure; time-on-task result marginal (one-tailed p=0.09).
